problems.title: The two KL directions can reverse the approximation ranking
problems.source_location: arXiv v4 Section 3.2, PDF p.7; compute_kl and intervention-evaluation call
claim: The paper defines \(D_{\rm KL}(Q_S\Vert P)\), where \(P\) is original chat and \(Q_S\) is modified output. The codeâ€™s log-target operation computes \(D_{\rm KL}(P\Vert Q_S)\).
analysis: Let \(P=(0.8,0.2)\), \(Q_A=(0.5,0.5)\), \(Q_B=(0.99,0.01)\). The specified divergences are about \(0.2231435513\) and \(0.1810049606\), preferring B; the released direction gives \(0.1927447570\) and \(0.4286718823\), preferring A. Every entry is positive and finite logits realize them. Adding identical positive tail mass to a larger vocabulary scales all divergences by the same positive factor and retains the reversal.
result: The metric correspondence is wrong in general. Both directions are legitimate choices; the example does not identify an actual Figure 4 reversal or show that codeâ€™s intended metric was intrinsically inappropriate.
repair: Either swap the evaluation arguments to follow the manuscript or revise the manuscriptâ€™s direction and associated interpretation to follow the code. Scalar averages cannot recover the opposite KL without underlying distributions.

problems.title: Variance depends on how the same observations are batched
claim: Batch variance uses default sample denominator \(n_b-1\), then merge code multiplies it by \(n_b\) as if it were population variance.
analysis: For observations \((0,2,4,6)\), the mean is \(3\), centered sum of squares \(20\), population variance \(5\), sample variance \(20/3\). One batch stores \(20/3\). Splitting into \((0,2)\), \((4,6)\) gives batch means \(1,5\), sample variances \(2,2\); the source merge returns \((2\cdot2+2\cdot2+16)/4=6\), neither correct convention. Singleton calls also create undefined batch sample variance although the pooled sample becomes defined.
result: The variance arithmetic is not partition-invariant and can change plotted uncertainty. Token dependence and interval coverage remain separate statistical questions.
repair: Store centered sum of squares \(M_2\). Merge using \(M_{2,A}+M_{2,B}+(\mu_B-\mu_A)^2n_An_B/(n_A+n_B)\), and divide only at readout by the chosen total denominator.
